source_review.notes: Checked all ten final NASA, NIST, and DoD references on 2026-08-31; every URL returned HTTP 200. Reviewed NASA closeout/Phase E/software retirement/technical data/configuration/review guidance, final NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 published September 2025, DoD materiel disposition and current policy listings, and NPR 7123.1B. NASA mission, NIST information-security, and DoD property/demilitarization scopes are explicit and require applicable legal/domain tailoring.

evidence: Reviewed typed closure graph and per-node disposition tuple for action, owner, authority, evidence, residual risk, retention, and state.
Reviewed closure implication requiring declared coverage, no open critical obligation, accepted transfers, and retrievable evidence.
Reviewed retirement scope by capability, effectivity, time, and authority, including relationship disposition.
Reviewed bounded sanitization claim by media, data, method, tool, verification, custody, and threat.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation distinguishes retirement decisions, discovered scope, dispositions, transfer acceptance, sanitization, residual ownership, and bounded closure.

evidence: Executed decommissioning-closure-fixture under python3 with exact output in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-089/report.json.
Confirmed eight declared domains, seven initially complete, and external_credentials as the sole open domain.
Confirmed revocation changes the declared ledger to eight complete and zero open domains while granting only metadata-gate eligibility.
Recomputed Exercise 2 known-ledger disposition coverage as 22/24 approximately 91.67 percent.
Recomputed an optimistic expanded denominator for at least one additional unknown object as no more than 22/25=88 percent.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Boolean ledger counts and coverage do not establish discovery completeness, evidence authenticity, authority, successor correctness, sanitization, custody, hazards, or closure.

evidence: Confirmed deactivation or power-off does not entail decommissioning or disposal completion.
Confirmed successor availability and zero recent traffic do not entail complete consumer migration.
Confirmed deletion, formatting, reset, encryption, sanitization, destruction, record disposition, and copy removal are distinct claims.
Confirmed property pickup or transfer does not entail sanitization, recipient technical acceptance, lawful downstream disposition, or liability closure.
Confirmed complete declared ledger coverage does not entail complete real-world scope without independent discovery and post-cutoff observation.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Implication limits prevent service, data, identity, property, archive, and checklist signals from becoming false closure proof.

evidence: Challenged seasonal/batch/failure-only/offline consumers, subsidiaries, field assets, spares/repairs, disaster recovery, external customers, suppliers, and unsupported populations.

Challenged databases, replicas, backups, snapshots, caches, queues, logs, exports, analytics/test/training copies, endpoints, paper, vendors, models, source/build artifacts, and archival format/tool dependencies.
Challenged service/machine accounts, tokens, keys, certificates, signing, DNS/routes/firewalls/VPN, automation, vendor/break-glass, physical access, cloud regions, registries, and billing remnants.

Challenged media-specific sanitization, failed/damaged devices, cryptographic-erase assumptions, provider visibility, custody chains, controlled/export-sensitive capability, hazardous material, contamination, environmental monitoring, and legal holds.
Reviewed all ten examples and five complete answers for assumptions, intermediate reasoning, positive/negative evidence, uncertainty, effectivity, residual ownership, and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real closure requires applicable systems/domain, operations, software/data/platform, identity/security/privacy, property/logistics, environmental/safety, suppliers/contracts, records/legal, finance, successor/customer, V&V, and technical-authority expertise.

evidence: Confirmed decision authority, effectivity, cutoff, success/abort criteria, continuity, records, property, environmental obligations, and residual owners precede execution.
Confirmed required operation and controls continue until the agreed cutoff while declared inventories are challenged by observation and inspection.
Confirmed every service, relationship, identity, information copy, physical asset, support capability, contract, hazard, and record receives owned disposition and evidence.
Confirmed successor transition and termination include acceptance, reconciliation, late/in-flight work, fallback, customer communication, and recovery.
Confirmed preservation and sanitization are purpose-, data-, media-, threat-, destination-, retention-, license-, and custody-specific.
Confirmed closure combines positive continuity/retrieval evidence, negative absence evidence, accepted residual ownership, post-close monitoring, and anomaly reopening.
invariant_checking.notes: No shutdown, replacement launch, traffic graph, delete command, factory reset, vendor certificate, pickup receipt, archive copy, disabled user list, or completed checklist is treated as sufficient alone.

proof_review.notes: No formal proof or theorem requires proof review; closure coverage and ledger logic are bounded governance mechanisms.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is labeled or presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Executable output is labeled declared_boolean_status_only.
Fixture limitations disclaim scope discovery, authentication, authority, transfer acceptance, sanitization, custody, observation, successor/archive tests, hazards, and closure.

Examples and exercises are synthetic teaching cases, not actual decommissioning approvals, sanitization certificates, property disposition, environmental clearance, legal advice, or successor acceptance.
Official sources are attributed without claiming NASA, NIST, or DoD review, approval, or endorsement of this chapter.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Synthetic ledger state, source-backed guidance, internal review, legal/property/environmental authority, technical closure, and operational evidence remain distinct.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked deactivation/decommissioning/retirement/disposal distinctions, authority/effectivity, operational integrity, closure inventory, consumers, successor transition, information copies and obligations, sanitization, identities, property/facilities, support, archives, negative evidence, reviews, measures, residual ownership, and design for exit.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked services/APIs/cloud, identities/network/automation, data migration/retention/sanitization, physical inventory and hazardous chains, field/spare/support obligations, facilities, suppliers/contracts/licenses, archives/records, closure evidence, post-cutoff monitoring, exceptions, and environmental/property/security custody.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from retirement authority and discovery through service/data/identity/property disposition, preservation, verification, residual ownership, and exit-ready design. Ten examples and five complete solutions cover hidden consumers, data copies, cloud remnants, media, facilities, field support, archives, PKI, controlled property, and ledger reopening.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external NASA/NIST/DoD expert, system/service owner, software/data/platform or identity/security/privacy specialist, media-sanitization assessor, property/logistics/export/demilitarization authority, environmental/safety specialist, supplier/vendor, contracts/IP/finance/records/legal authority, successor/customer, V&V authority, auditor, or other external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
